 Audio Bose recalls over 670,000 S1 Pro speaker batteries after reports of fires and property damage
 You can still use your speaker without the affected battery. Hillary Keverenge • Nov 16, 2026 — 5:51 AM ET 
 • • Bose Add Android Authority on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover TL;DR 
 Bose has issued a recall affecting over 670,000 battery packs for its S1 Pro and S1 Pro Plus Bluetooth speakers in the US and Canada.
 The batteries can become a fire hazard as they age, with seven incidents and six reports of property damage recorded so far.
 Bose is offering free replacement batteries, and owners can continue using their speakers on AC power after removing the affected batteries.
 Buying a premium Bluetooth speaker from a brand like Bose usually comes with the expectation that it’ll serve you well for years. However, owners of the Bose S1 Pro and S1 Pro Plus may want to take a closer look at their speakers, especially if they’ve had them for a while, because Bose has issued a major recall affecting both models after discovering that their batteries can become a fire hazard as they age.
 The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced the recall earlier this month (via Tom’s Guide ), affecting approximately 670,000 battery packs across the US and Canada . The safety concerns aren’t merely precautionary, either. Bose has already received seven reports of batteries melting, producing smoke, or catching fire, with six incidents resulting in property damage. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported.
 Bose This isn’t the first time Bose has had to address a fire hazard involving its audio products. In June 2023, the company recalled approximately 884,000 bass modules in the US after their electrical components were found to be susceptible to failure. In December 2024, Anker also recalled around 69,000 Soundcore and PowerConf Bluetooth speakers following 33 reports of battery overheating, including one minor burn injury.
 However, there’s some good news for anyone who spent $700 on either of the affected Bose S1 Pro or S1 Pro Plus speakers. Unlike Anker customers who had to replace their entire speakers, Bose owners only need a new battery, which the company is providing free of charge.
 Owners should immediately remove and stop using the affected batteries. To determine whether yours is included in the recall, look for the 17-digit serial number on the battery’s underside.
 Bose Affected batteries have serial numbers beginning with:
 083723
 078352
 084105
 078591
 078592
 084106
 086409
 You can claim a free replacement through Bose’s recall website or by calling 800-278-1083 in the US. Contact your local hazardous waste collection facility for disposal instructions, as recalled batteries cannot go into household trash or regular battery recycling bins.
 The recall covers products sold in the US between December 2017 and July 2026, including batteries purchased separately. So, remember to check any spares you have lying around, too.
 In the meantime, you don’t have to put your music on hold. Both Bose speakers can still be used safely when plugged into a wall outlet with the affected battery removed.
